info.title: MSP API
info.description: Multi-sport competition platform. Errors are Problem Details with a stable `code` (contracts/errors.json) and the request's `correlationId`.

get.description: Active ISO 3166-1 countries, ordered by alpha-2 code. Cacheable for an hour; send the `ETag` back as `If-None-Match` to get 304.
Active ISO 4217 currencies (money only), ordered by code, with their minor units. Cacheable for an hour; send the `ETag` back as `If-None-Match` to get 304.
Active ISO 639-1 languages, ordered by code. Cacheable for an hour; send the `ETag` back as `If-None-Match` to get 304.

Active IANA time zones, ordered by ID. `country` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, upper case) keeps only that country's zones; a country without zones gives an empty list. Cacheable for an hour; send the `ETag` back as `If-None-Match` to get 304.

The tenant whose site this host serves: slug, display name and primary domain. The tenant comes from the request host (`X-Forwarded-Host` from a trusted proxy). Responses differ per host. Cacheable for a minute; send the `ETag` back as `If-None-Match` to get 304.
The settings of the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`, with their `version` (also the `ETag`).

ETag.description: The resource's `version`, quoted (a strong entity tag). Send it back as `If-Match`.

patch.description: Changes the keys sent of the settings of the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`; missing or null keys stay as they are. Any other key, or a value of the wrong type, is 400 VALIDATION_INVALID_REQUEST with an `errors` entry naming it. Send `version` from the last read to get 409 TENANT_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT instead of overwriting someone else's change; `If-Match` with the `ETag` works the same way (if both are sent, both must match).

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The `ETag` of the last read (or `*`). If the resource changed since, the change fails with 409 `*_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT`; a body `version`, if also sent, must match too.

ETag.description: The resource's `version`, quoted (a strong entity tag). Send it back as `If-Match`.

get.description: The status and access mode of the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`, with the reason and time of the change that put it in that status, the tenant's time zone, and the current subscription period's status and days (`null` without a period). Available while the tenant is suspended or archived, so its owner sees why every other request is `403 TENANT_BLOCKED`, and while it is read-only, when writes are `403 TENANT_READ_ONLY`.

The subscription of the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`: the current period (plan, kind, status today and days, all in the tenant's time zone; `null` without a period) and the next scheduled one; every entitlement's value today with its source (DEFAULT, PLAN or OVERRIDE); and every quota's usage (`used` of `limit`, `null` = unlimited; `warning` from 80 % of the limit; `measured: false` while no module counts it yet). Available while the tenant is read-only. To change the plan, the tenant contacts the platform.

The members of the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`, oldest first, with their email and active roles. Filter by `status` (ACTIVE, SUSPENDED or REMOVED); without it, removed members are left out. `limit` is 1–100 (25). Every page read is audited.
A member of the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`, with their active roles and `version` (also the `ETag`).

ETag.description: The resource's `version`, quoted (a strong entity tag). Send it back as `If-Match`.

post.description: ACTIVE → SUSPENDED, with a reason: the member loses access to the tenant and keeps their roles. Only an owner changes an owner, and the last active owner can't be suspended or removed. The body `{ "reason": … }` is required. The reason is kept permanently on the membership and in the audit trail: don't include personal data. Send `version` or `If-Match` from the last read to get 409 AUTH_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT if the member changed since.

Only an owner grants TENANT_OWNER. Returns the member. Send `version` or `If-Match` from the last read to get 409 AUTH_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT if the member changed since.

Returns the member. Send `version` or `If-Match` from the last read to get 409 AUTH_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT if the member changed since.

post.summary: Invite a person to the tenant
post.description: Invites `email` to join the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id` with `roleCodes` (tenant roles, tenant-wide). Only an owner invites with TENANT_OWNER or replaces a pending invitation that has it. A person who is already a member (active or suspended) can't be invited. Every member who isn't removed and every pending invitation takes one of the plan's staff users (MAX_STAFF_USERS); an invitation past the limit is ENTITLEMENT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED, and one that replaces a pending invitation to the same email adds no one. The invitation lasts 7 days; the email with its link goes out shortly after (one link at a time: a resent email's link replaces the earlier one). A pending invitation to the same email is revoked and replaced.

ETag.description: The resource's `version`, quoted (a strong entity tag). Send it back as `If-Match`.

get.description: The invitations of the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`, oldest first, with their email, roles and status. Filter by `status` (PENDING, EXPIRED, ACCEPTED or REVOKED); without it, the ones still pending, expired ones included. `limit` is 1–100 (25). Every page read is audited.
An invitation of the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`, with its email, roles, status and `version` (also the `ETag`).

ETag.description: The resource's `version`, quoted (a strong entity tag). Send it back as `If-Match`.

post.description: PENDING → REVOKED: the invitation's link stops working. An accepted, revoked or expired invitation can't be revoked; only an owner revokes one with TENANT_OWNER. Sending its email changes its version, so a revoke may get 409 once while the email goes out. The body is optional. Returns the invitation. Send `version` or `If-Match` from the last read to get 409 AUTH_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT if the invitation changed since.

parameters.description: The `ETag` of the last read (or `*`). If the resource changed since, the change fails with 409 `*_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT`; a body `version`, if also sent, must match too.

get.summary: List the tenant actions the signed-in user may perform, and those the tenant can't use now
get.description: What the signed-in user's roles grant in the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id` (tenant actions, docs/generated/actions.md). Without `scopeType`/`scopeId`, the actions granted tenant-wide; with them (COMPETITION, TEAM or CONTEST and its ID), also those granted on that resource or the scopes above it. `actions`: what the user may perform now, in ordinal order. `unavailable`: what the roles grant but the tenant can't use now, each with the refusal a request would get: TENANT_READ_ONLY (the subscription has ended, was cancelled or hasn't started) or ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED (with the entitlement and the plans that include it, for "Requires PRO plan"). Actions the roles don't grant are in neither list. `access`: the tenant's access mode, the current subscription period's status and last days (null without a period) and the tenant's time zone, for the banner. The admin app shows only what `actions` allows and disables what `unavailable` lists; every request is still authorized. A read-only tenant answers this request; a blocked one, or a provisioning one for a member who can't set it up, answers 403 with the reason (TENANT_BLOCKED, TENANT_PROVISIONING).

Every published sport variant at its latest version, ordered by name, then variant code: its sport, scoring family, contest shape and latest version. Not paginated. Not audited (global configuration).

A variant's published definition (docs/domain/sports/README.md) at `version`, the latest when left out: terminology, periods, actor roles, event types and the generic event types every definition has, positions, staff and official roles, lineup, statistics and the scorer pad. A published version never changes. Labels are the definition's; show them as given. Not audited (global configuration).

ETag.description: The definition's `contentHash`, quoted: it changes only with a new version.

get.description: Outbox messages of every module, newest first, without their payloads. Filter by `module` (a module schema) and `status` (PENDING, PROCESSED or FAILED); `limit` is 1–100 (25). `heldBackBy` names the earlier message a PENDING one waits for.

post.description: Moves one FAILED message back to PENDING with its attempts reset; the processor delivers it on its next poll. Fix the cause first: a message that fails again ends FAILED again. The reason is kept permanently in the audit trail: don't include personal data.

get.description: Audit entries of every tenant, newest first. Filter by `tenantId`, `actorId`, `action` (an action code), `entityType` and `entityId` (`entityId` needs `entityType`), `correlationId`, `outcome` (SUCCESS, FAILURE or DENIED), and `from` (inclusive) / `to` (exclusive), ISO 8601 instants with an offset (encode `+` as `%2B`); `limit` is 1–100 (25). Entries recorded through a module's outbox arrive shortly after the action, so one can appear before a page already read. Every page read is itself audited: don't poll this list.

post.description: Invites `email` to join the tenant as TENANT_OWNER, usually while it is PROVISIONING; an ARCHIVED tenant is refused. A person who is already a member can't be invited. The invitation lasts 7 days; the email with its link goes out shortly after (one link at a time: a resent email's link replaces the earlier one). A pending invitation to the same email is revoked and replaced.

ETag.description: The resource's `version`, quoted (a strong entity tag). Send it back as `If-Match`.

get.description: Every tenant, ordered by slug. Filter by `status` (PROVISIONING, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED or ARCHIVED); `limit` is 1–100 (25). Every page read is audited.

post.description: Creates a tenant in PROVISIONING. `slug` (3–40 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, not a reserved word) names its platform subdomain, never changes and is never reused, even after the tenant is archived. Country, time zone, locale (`en` or `en-UG`) and currency must be active reference data. `publicEnabled` defaults to false; the public site shows only while the tenant is ACTIVE.

ETag.description: The resource's `version`, quoted (a strong entity tag). Send it back as `If-Match`.

get.description: One tenant with its profile, status, main settings and `version` (also the `ETag`). The version is the tenant row's only: a settings change doesn't change it.

ETag.description: The resource's `version`, quoted (a strong entity tag). Send it back as `If-Match`.

patch.description: Changes the fields sent; missing or null fields stay as they are. The slug never changes, and the status changes only through the status actions. Send `version` from the last read to get 409 TENANT_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT instead of overwriting someone else's change; `If-Match` with the `ETag` works the same way (if both are sent, both must match). The version is the tenant row's only: a settings change made since your read (here or through the admin settings endpoint) is not detected.

get.description: Every subscription period of the tenant, latest start first, with its status on `today` (the tenant's date), the current period (the one that decides access) and the next scheduled one. Statuses are derived from the dates: SCHEDULED, ACTIVE, EXPIRING, GRACE, EXPIRED or CANCELLED.

post.summary: Give a tenant a subscription period
post.description: A new period on `planCode` (an active plan; otherwise TENANT_PLAN_NOT_FOUND on the field) from `startsOn` to `endsOn`. Dates are the tenant's (its time zone in settings) and both `startsOn` and `endsOn` are included. `kind` (PAID, TRIAL or COMPLIMENTARY) is for reporting only. `expiringWindowDays` defaults to 30 and `graceDays` to 14 (0–365). A period that shares a day with another period that isn't cancelled is refused (TENANT_SUBSCRIPTION_OVERLAP). A trial, an event pass or the pilot offer is an ordinary period.

A new period from the day after the latest period (that isn't cancelled) ends, or from today if that day has passed or every period is cancelled, to `endsOn`. Dates are the tenant's (its time zone in settings) and both `startsOn` and `endsOn` are included. `planCode`, `kind` and the windows not sent are the latest period's: a lower plan is chosen here. Without any period, TENANT_SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND (assign one instead); an `endsOn` before the first day, VALIDATION_INVALID_REQUEST on `endsOn`; no `planCode` while the latest period's plan is no longer active, TENANT_PLAN_NOT_FOUND on `planCode`.

post.summary: Move a tenant to a higher plan now
post.description: Cancels the current period (reason "Changed to <plan>") and adds one on `planCode` from today to the same `endsOn`, with the same kind and windows; the history keeps both. Only to a higher plan (TENANT_SUBSCRIPTION_DOWNGRADE_AT_RENEWAL otherwise: choose a lower plan when renewing), and only while the current period is ACTIVE or EXPIRING (TENANT_SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND otherwise: renew instead).

Cancels, now and with `reason`, every period that isn't cancelled or expired: those in effect today (an earlier one still in GRACE included) and every scheduled one. Nothing to cancel is TENANT_SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND. The reason is kept permanently on the periods and in the audit trail: don't include personal data.

post.summary: Give a tenant its own value of an entitlement
post.description: `value` in place of the plan's for `entitlementCode` (a declared entitlement, GET /api/platform/v1/plans), of its type: `{"enabled": true}`, `{"limit": 5}` (`null` = unlimited) or `{"level": "FULL"}` (`null` = none); otherwise TENANT_OVERRIDE_INVALID_VALUE on the field. It applies until `effectiveUntil` (the tenant's date, included; on or after its today, else VALIDATION_INVALID_REQUEST on the field) or, without one, until it is removed. An override already in place for the entitlement is removed ("Replaced by a new override") in the same change; the history keeps both. The reason is kept permanently on the override and in the audit trail, and tenants never see it: don't include personal data.

Removes the override now, with `reason`: the plan's value applies again. An override the tenant doesn't have, or one already removed (or replaced), is TENANT_OVERRIDE_NOT_FOUND. The reason is kept permanently on the override and in the audit trail, and tenants never see it: don't include personal data.

get.description: The active plans in rank order (then by code), each with every entitlement's definition and value, ordered by entitlement code. A value is `{ enabled }`, `{ limit }` (null = unlimited) or `{ level }` (null = none); `value` itself is null when the configuration seed hasn't written that entitlement yet (not "unlimited"). Plans change only through a reviewed seed (no editing). Every read is audited.

get.summary: List the platform actions the signed-in user may perform
get.description: The codes of the platform actions (docs/generated/actions.md) the signed-in user's platform roles grant, in ordinal order. The platform console shows only what this list allows; every request is still authorized.

Every published sport variant at its latest version, ordered by name, then variant code: its sport, scoring family, contest shape and latest version. Not paginated. Not audited (global configuration).

A variant's published definition (docs/domain/sports/README.md) at `version`, the latest when left out: terminology, periods, actor roles, event types and the generic event types every definition has, positions, staff and official roles, lineup, statistics and the scorer pad. A published version never changes. Labels are the definition's; show them as given. Not audited (global configuration).

ETag.description: The definition's `contentHash`, quoted: it changes only with a new version.

post.description: Signs in with email and password and starts a session: the response sets the session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict; 12 hours sliding, 7 days at most). An unknown email, a wrong password, a locked or unconfirmed account all answer `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS`. Five wrong passwords lock the account for 15 minutes. Limited to 20 attempts a minute per client address and 10 per 15 minutes per email (`AUTH_RATE_LIMITED`, with `Retry-After`). Needs `X-CSRF: 1` like every other change.
Ends this session and deletes the session cookie.

get.description: The signed-in user: ID, email, active platform roles, and the tenants they are an active member of, ordered by name, each with its slug, display name and status and the user's roles there. Every status is listed. A suspended or archived tenant's workspace is blocked (TENANT_BLOCKED): only `tenant.access.read` is allowed. A provisioning tenant's workspace opens only for those setting it up; others get TENANT_PROVISIONING.

post.summary: Ask for a password reset email
post.description: Sends a password reset link to the email if it belongs to an account. Always answers 202, whether or not it does. The link works once, for 1 hour, and only the newest link works. Limited to 10 requests an hour per client address and 3 an hour per email (`AUTH_RATE_LIMITED`, with `Retry-After`). Needs `X-CSRF: 1`.

post.summary: Set a new password with a reset token
post.description: Sets a new password with the token from a reset email's link. The token works once, for 1 hour, and only the newest one works; otherwise `AUTH_RESET_TOKEN_INVALID`. The new password needs at least 12 characters (`AUTH_PASSWORD_REJECTED`, the rule in `detail`). Signs out every session of the user and clears a lockout; it does not sign in. Needs `X-CSRF: 1`.

Changes the signed-in user's password. A wrong current password answers `AUTH_CURRENT_PASSWORD_INVALID` and counts toward the lockout (five lock the account for 15 minutes). The new password needs at least 12 characters (`AUTH_PASSWORD_REJECTED`, the rule in `detail`). The user's other sessions end within 5 minutes; this one stays (the response renews its cookie). Needs `X-CSRF: 1`.

post.summary: Look up an invitation by its token
post.description: What an invitation link is for: the tenant, the invited email and roles, when it expires, and whether the email has an account (then sign in with it before accepting; otherwise choose a password when accepting). The token from the email's link goes in the body. An unknown, revoked or replaced token is `AUTH_INVITATION_TOKEN_INVALID`; an expired invitation `AUTH_INVITATION_EXPIRED`; an accepted one `AUTH_INVITATION_ALREADY_ACCEPTED`. Anonymous callers allowed; needs `X-CSRF: 1`.

Joins the invitation's tenant with its roles. If the invited email has no account, send `password` (at least 12 characters, `AUTH_PASSWORD_REJECTED`): the account is created with that password. If it has one, sign in with it first (`AUTH_INVITATION_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED` otherwise); `password` is then ignored. The token works once and the same refusals as the lookup apply; a current member gets `AUTH_ALREADY_MEMBER`. Does not sign in. Anonymous callers allowed; needs `X-CSRF: 1`.

AcceptInvitationRequest.description:
The token from an invitation email's link, and the password to set when the invited email has no account yet
(ignored when it has one: the invitee is signed in as that user instead).

AcceptInvitationResponse.description: The membership the invitee now holds; they sign in to use it (accepting doesn't sign in).

ActorPool.description: Who may fill an actor role.

ActorSide.description: Whose side, relative to the event's side.

AssignmentScope.description: A role assignment scope that can grant a tenant action.

AssignPeriodRequest.description:
A new period: `planCode` from `startsOn` to `endsOn` (both included, the tenant's dates). The windows
default to 30 expiring and 14 grace days.

AssignRoleRequest.description:
A role to give a member: its code and scope (`TENANT` when not sent; the only scope S03 accepts, so
`scopeId` stays empty). `version`, when sent, must be the membership's current one.

AuditEntryResponse.description:
One audit entry as platform staff see it: every column, with `metadata` as the JSON object it was stored as
(personal data already masked when it was recorded).

CancelSubscriptionRequest.description:
The body of `subscription.cancel` (audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`). The reason is kept permanently on the
cancelled periods and in the audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.

CapabilitiesResponse.description:
The platform action codes the caller may perform, in ordinal order; Scope is always null (kept so
the platform list has the shape it had in S03). The tenant list is TenantCapabilitiesResponse.

CapabilityAccessResponse.description:
The tenant's access today, for the shell's banner: the access `mode`; the current subscription period's status,
first day, last day, last day of grace and the day it was cancelled (all null without a period; `cancelledOn`
null unless it was cancelled), so the banner can say since when a tenant is read-only; the tenant's `timeZone`
(IANA), in which the days begin and end. A response of its own, so a field added to Tenancy's contract doesn't change
the API.

CapabilityScopeResponse.description: The resource the capabilities were asked about.

ChangeMemberStatusRequest.description: The optional body of `restore`: `version`, when sent, must be the membership's current one.

ChangeMemberStatusWithReasonRequest.description:
The body of `suspend` and `remove` (audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`). The reason is kept permanently on
the membership and in the audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.

ChangePlanRequest.description: The higher plan to move to now.

ChangeTenantStatusRequest.description: The optional body of `activate` and `restore`: `version`, when sent, must be the tenant's current one.

ChangeTenantStatusWithReasonRequest.description:
The body of `suspend`, `archive` and `unarchive` (audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`). The reason is kept
permanently in the status history and the audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.

CountryResponse.description: An ISO 3166-1 country: alpha-2 `code` (`UG`), alpha-3, numeric code and English name.

CoverageLevel.description: In order: a level includes every level before it.

CreateTenantRequest.description:
A new tenant. Every field but `publicEnabled` (default false) is required; unknown members are rejected,
so a status can't be sent (a new tenant is always `PROVISIONING`).

CurrencyResponse.description: An ISO 4217 currency: alphabetic `code` (`UGX`), numeric code, English name, minor units (UGX 0).

EffectiveEntitlementResponse.description:
A tenant's value of one entitlement today and where it comes from: `DEFAULT`, `PLAN` (the current period's
plan) or `OVERRIDE` (an unremoved override in effect).

EntitlementOverrideResponse.description:
One entitlement override: `value` in place of the plan's for `entitlementCode`, until `effectiveUntil`
(included; none = until removed). `inEffect`: it applies on the response's `today` (not removed, not past
its last day). The removal fields are set together.

EntitlementSource.description: Where a tenant's effective value of an entitlement comes from (S04 D6).

EntitlementType.description: What kind of value an entitlement has (docs/architecture/authorization.md, "Entitlements").

limit.description: QUOTA: the most items; null = unlimited.

level.description: LEVEL: a level code; null = none.

EntitlementValue.description: An entitlement's value, by its type: `{ enabled }` (BOOLEAN), `{ limit }` (QUOTA; null = unlimited) or `{ level }` (LEVEL; null = none).

ForgotPasswordRequest.description: Ask for a password reset email.

GrantOverrideRequest.description:
The body of `entitlement.override` (audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`): `value` in place of the plan's for
`entitlementCode`, until `effectiveUntil` (the tenant's date, included; none = until removed). The reason
is kept permanently in the override and the audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.

InvitationResponse.description:
An invitation as the admin API shows it. `status` is `EXPIRED` for a pending one past `expiresAt`. The
email is shown to every holder of `membership.read`, like a member's (owner, S03-T4b), and never logged or
audited. `version` (also the `ETag`) changes whenever the invitation does, a resent email included.

InvitationState.description:
An invitation as people see it: the stored status, with InvitationState.Expired derived from a pending invitation's
`expires_at` (S03 D12). Never stored.

InviteMemberRequest.description: Invite a person to the tenant: their email and the tenant roles they get, tenant-wide.

LanguageResponse.description: An ISO 639-1 language: two-letter `code` (`sw`) and English name.

LoginRequest.description: Sign in with email and password.

LookupInvitationRequest.description: The token from an invitation email's link, in the body so request logs and traces never hold it.

LookupInvitationResponse.description:
A pending invitation as its invitee sees it: the tenant's display name, the invited email (the token proves the
invitee holds it), the tenant-wide roles, when it expires, and whether the email has an account: if it does, the
invitee signs in with it before accepting; if not, they choose a password when accepting.

MemberResponse.description:
A member of the tenant as the admin API shows them, with their active roles. The email is the user's only
identifier until people have profiles; shown to every holder of `membership.read` (owner, S03-T4b) and never
logged or audited. `version` (also the `ETag`) is the membership's; role changes change it too.

MemberRoleResponse.description: An active role assignment: the role, where it applies (`scopeId` null tenant-wide) and when it was granted.

MeResponse.description: The signed-in user: their own email, platform roles and the tenants they are an active member of.

MetadataFieldResponse.description: A metadata field: `values` for a choice, `min` and `max` for a number.

MetadataValueType.description:
A metadata field's type in the API (`CHOICE`, `FLAG`, `NUMBER`, `TEXT`); the files write
`enum`, `bool`, `int` and `string`.

MeTenantResponse.description:
A tenant the user is an active member of: its slug (the workspace URL), display name and status, and the codes of the
roles they hold there (any scope). Every status is listed. A `SUSPENDED` or `ARCHIVED` tenant's workspace is
blocked, and its owner can read why; a `PROVISIONING` tenant's opens only for those setting it up (others get
`TENANT_PROVISIONING`).

MinorRegistrationConsent.description:
Whether a guardian's consent is needed before a minor is registered for a competition (Q11). Consent before public
exposure is always required, whatever this says.

OutboxMessageResponse.description:
One outbox message in the platform diagnostics: envelope and delivery state, no payload. `heldBackBy` is set on
a `PENDING` message that waits for an earlier, not yet processed message of its aggregate.

OutboxMessageStatus.description: Delivery status of an outbox message (docs/domain/state-machines.md, "Outbox message").

PageInfo.description:
The `page` member of a cursor-paginated list (docs/architecture/api-conventions.md): pass
NextCursor as `cursor` to get the next page; it is null on the last page.

PeriodResponse.description: A period; `shortLabel` is the definition's short form (`1H`).

PlanEntitlementResponse.description:
An entitlement's definition and its Value on the plan: null when the stored plan has no value for
it yet (the code declares an entitlement that `seed --category CONFIGURATION` hasn't written).

code.description: Stable error code, `<AREA>_<CONDITION>` (contracts/errors.json). Clients branch on it.

correlationId.description: The request's correlation ID (also the `X-Correlation-Id` response header).

errors.description: Validation failures, one per field: `field` (camelCase) and `code`.

QuotaUsageResponse.description:
One quota's usage (S04 D15): `used` of `limit` (null = unlimited) when a module measures it
(`measured`); otherwise `used` is null: not measured yet. `warning`: the tenant uses 80 % of the
limit or more.

RedriveOutboxMessageRequest.description:
Why the message is re-driven; the audit entry records it (action audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`). Kept permanently
and not redacted, so it must not contain personal data.

RemoveOverrideRequest.description:
The body of `entitlement.override.remove` (audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`). The reason is kept permanently on
the override and in the audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.

RenewSubscriptionRequest.description:
A renewal up to `endsOn` (included). The plan, kind and windows not sent are the latest period's; a lower plan
is chosen here.

ResetPasswordRequest.description: Set a new password with the token from a reset email's link.

RevokeInvitationRequest.description: The optional body of `revoke`: `version`, when sent, must be the invitation's current one.

RevokeRoleRequest.description: The optional body of `revoke`: `version`, when sent, must be the membership's current one.

SiteResponse.description:
The public site's identity: `PUBLIC` fields only. PrimaryDomain is the host the site
prefers, which may differ from the host the request came in on.

SportDefinitionResponse.description:
A published sport definition as the API shows it: the definition's content (docs/domain/sports/README.md) in the API's
names (camelCase, UPPER_SNAKE values), with its version's hash and publication time and the generic event types.
Actor roles and metadata fields stay maps keyed by their codes, as in the file.

StatisticDerivationResponse.description: How a statistic is derived; `where` holds metadata conditions, each value as written.

SubscriptionKind.description: How a period was granted; for reporting only, never affects its status or access (state-machines.md).

SubscriptionPeriodResponse.description:
One period: `startsOn` to `endsOn`, both days included. `expiringFrom` is the first day of
`EXPIRING` (after `endsOn` when the window is 0), `graceEndsOn` the last day of `GRACE`. The
cancellation fields are set together.

SubscriptionResponse.description:
A tenant's subscription as the platform sees it (S04 D16): every period, latest start first, with its status on
`today`, the tenant's date in `timeZone`. `currentPeriodId` is the period that decides access (none
without periods); `nextPeriodId` the next scheduled one. `overrides` are the tenant's entitlement overrides
with their reasons and history, unremoved first (S04 D5): platform-only. `entitlements` are every declared
entitlement's effective value today, by code, with its source (D6). `usage` is every quota's usage, as the
owning module counts it (D15; "not measured yet" when none does).

SubscriptionStatus.description:
A subscription period's status, derived from its stored dates on a given day (docs/domain/state-machines.md,
"Subscription period"); never stored.

TenantAccessMode.description: What a tenant may do, derived from its status and its current subscription period: state-machines.md.

TenantAccessPeriod.description:
The current subscription period on `/tenant/access`: its status today and its days (all included), in the
tenant's time zone. `graceEndsOn` is the last day of grace; equal to `endsOn` when the period has no grace
days. A response of its own, so a field added to Tenancy's contract for other modules doesn't change the API (#66 R4).

TenantAccessResponse.description:
A tenant's access as its owner sees it: `status`; the `accessMode` derived from it and the current
subscription period; the `reason` (null when the change needs none, such as an activation) and time
(`since`) of the change that put the tenant in its status; the tenant's `timeZone` (IANA), in which to show
`since` and the period's days; and the current period's status and days (`subscription`, null without a
period). A read-only tenant's `subscription` says why; the cancel reason is the platform's and is not shown.

TenantCapabilitiesResponse.description:
The tenant capabilities (S04 D14): `actions`, the action codes the caller may perform now (all three steps of
the decision formula), in ordinal order; `unavailable`, the actions the caller's roles grant but the tenant
can't use now, with the reason, in ordinal order; `access`, the tenant's access for the banner;
`scope`, the resource asked about, if any. Actions the roles don't grant are in neither list.

TenantEntitlementResponse.description:
One entitlement as the tenant's Subscription page shows it: its name, description, type, unit (quotas) and levels
(level entitlements, lowest first), and the tenant's value today with its source (`DEFAULT`, `PLAN` or
`OVERRIDE`).

TenantListItem.description:
A tenant in the platform list. No settings: the list runs under no tenant, and settings are tenant-owned (read one
tenant for them). `version` is the tenant row's, as in the detail.

TenantResponse.description:
A tenant as the platform API shows it: the tenant and its main settings. Read under the tenant (the settings are
tenant-owned). `version` (also the `ETag`), `createdAt` and `updatedAt` are the tenant row's
only: a settings change doesn't change them, so the same `ETag` can come with different settings. Send
`version` back with a change to make it fail with `409 TENANT_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT` if someone else changed
the tenant first. The settings have their own version at `/api/admin/v1/tenant/settings`.

TenantSettingsResponse.description:
A tenant's settings as the admin API shows them. `version` (also the `ETag`) and `updatedAt` are the
settings row's, not the tenant's: send `version` back with a change to make it fail with
`409 TENANT_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT` if someone else changed the settings first.

TenantSubscriptionPeriod.description:
A period's plan (code and name), kind and status today, and its days, all included: `expiringFrom` is the first
day of `EXPIRING` (after `endsOn` when the window is 0), `graceEndsOn` the last day of `GRACE`.

TenantSubscriptionResponse.description:
A tenant's subscription as its members see it (S04 D15): `today` in the tenant's `timeZone`; the
`current` period (the one that decides access; null without periods) and the `next` scheduled one; every
declared entitlement's effective value with its source; and every quota's usage. No override reasons, cancel
reasons or who made a change: those are the platform's.

TimeZoneResponse.description: An IANA time zone: its ID as `code` (`Africa/Kampala`) and its country; no country for `Etc/UTC`.

UnavailableActionResponse.description:
An action the caller's roles grant that the tenant can't use now. `code` is the refusal the request would get
first: `TENANT_READ_ONLY` (step 1) or `ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED` (step 2). For `ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED`,
`entitlement` is the entitlement the action names and `plans` the active plans, in rank order, that include
it (empty when none does); both are null for `TENANT_READ_ONLY`.

UpdateTenantProfileRequest.description:
The profile fields to change; a missing or null field stays as it is. The slug and the status can't be changed here
(unknown members are rejected). `version`, when sent, must be the tenant's current version.

UpdateTenantSettingsRequest.description:
The settings to change; a missing or null key stays as it is. Only these keys exist: any other key, or a value of
the wrong type, is named in `errors`. `version`, when sent, must be the settings' current version.
